title: Extension by zero commutes with arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $U' \xrightarrow{g_U} U$ and $X' \xrightarrow{g} X$ form a cartesian square of schemes in which $j:U\to X$ and $j':U'\to X'$ are open immersions. For every abelian sheaf F on U_Et, the canonical base-change morphism

 g^{-1} j_! F → j'_! g_U^{-1} F

is an isomorphism; it is the inverse of the adjunction mate, under j'_! ⊣ j'^{-1}, of the composite g_U^{-1}F → g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F ≅ j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F, using the unit of j_! ⊣ j^{-1} and the cartesian identification j'^{-1}g^{-1} ≅ g_U^{-1}j^{-1}. For a finite commutative ring Λ and a complex of Λ-module sheaves, the corresponding map is an isomorphism degreewise.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point x̄' of X' and put x̄ = g∘x̄'. By the stalk formula for extension by zero, (j_!F)_x̄ is F_ū when x̄ = j∘ū for a geometric point ū of U, and is zero otherwise; the same formula gives (j'_!g_U^{-1}F)_x̄' as (g_U^{-1}F)_ū' on U' and zero outside U'.

source.place: Proposition 03S5 (etale-cohomology-proposition-describe-jshriek) and proof; Modules on Sites Lemma 0710

proof.text: Because the square is cartesian, x̄ lies in U exactly when x̄' lies in U', and in that case the chosen lift ū' maps to ū and the inverse-image stalk identification gives F_ū ≅ (g_U^{-1}F)_ū'. The canonical base-change morphism (the inverse of the adjunction mate) restricts on these stalks to this inverse identification, and restricts to the zero map between zero stalks in the complementary case. Thus the base-change morphism is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk.
Geometric stalks are conservative for morphisms of etale abelian sheaves, so the base-change morphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, final appeal to geometric-stalk conservativity

proof.text: For a finite commutative ring Λ, the constructions on complexes are degreewise. Applying the abelian-sheaf isomorphism to each term of a complex of Λ-module sheaves gives the asserted degreewise isomorphism (and the component maps commute with the differentials by functoriality).

source.place: Definition 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), which defines extension by zero on complexes degreewise
